artifacts.summary: Six-phase plan adding invariant C26 to scripts/check-module-invariants.sh, closing all four defsWithUnderscore evasion routes with one tree-wide textual scan plus a nolint-attribute allow-list, four deliberate negative tests, and append-only documentation.

memory_candidates.content: A linter that observes a package by IMPORTING it (Lean/Batteries env_linter, Mathlib's defsWithUnderscore) is structurally blind to two whole classes of declaration, and no amount of reconfiguring it helps: (a) private declarations, which are not exported to an importing module and so are simply absent from the environment the linter walks; (b) declarations in modules outside the lint target's import closure -- e.g. a module whose only importer is a lean_exe root. A third, softer blind spot is any heuristic the upstream linter applies to skip 'autogenerated' names (Mathlib skips names whose last component ends in _1/_2/_mathlib), which is invisible at the declaration site. A fourth is an in-source suppression attribute, which produces no finding at all and so is invisible to the linter, to CI, and to a suppression-baseline diff alike -- unlike a JSON baseline entry, which is at least a reviewable line. The general lesson: when a gate must cover private or out-of-closure code, the instrument has to be structurally different from the one being supplemented -- a repo-local TEXTUAL scan over the source tree, which consults no import closure and no visibility modifier, closes the private and out-of-closure routes in a single pass and can decline to inherit the upstream heuristic. One textual pass closes all four routes; four separate mechanisms is the wrong decomposition.
